newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russia's Gazprom needs credit to expand gas fields.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom needs credit to expand gas fields.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom said on Friday that it needs around 40.6 billion marks ($24 billion) to complete its gas field developments and that it could not meet these financial requirements solely through new share issues.
Gazprom Chairman Rem Vyakhirev said that the group needed credit finance for optimum growth.

He was speaking to journalists in Frankfurt as he signed an agreement between Gazprom and an international banking consortium, led by Germany's Dresdner Bank AG, offering the company a $2.5 billion loan facility.
The group plans to use the loan to finance the construction of Russia's Yamal pipeline to Western Europe.

Gazprom also received a further 1.5 billion marks in debt from a consortium under the joint leadership of Dresdner Bank and Deutsche Bank, which Gazprom will use to finance the purchase of natural gas equipment from Mannesmann.
Dresdner said the credit established Gazprom as an independent company on international capital markets, which no longer required government guarantees to raise credits.
The bank said it had received offers of funds totalling $7.5 billion from 19 banks in the arrangement process.
A spokesman for Dresdner would not specify the scale of Dresdner's share in the consortium, but said it was bigger than that of the other banks.
The credit has a maturity of eight years and bears an interest rate of two percent over LIBOR, or London Interbank Offered Rate.
Vyakhirev said the credit was secured on Gazprom's long-term gas sales contracts with Western European gas companies currently serviced by the existing pipeline grid.
Vyakhirev said that only nine percent of Gazprom shares can be placed with foreign investors under a Russian law aimed at protecting the country's natural resources.
At the moment around 40 percent of the company is in state hands, with around one percent of stock in foreign ownership and the rest in the hands of Russian investors.
There had been speculation earlier that Gazprom was planning to widen its stock ownership base to include more foreign investors, following a Wall Street Journal Europe report.
However, Gazprom later denied the report, saying its foreign share buying rules were unchanged and that it would take action against any breach of them.

In October, Gazprom listed some of its shares on a number of foreign bourses, including Berlin. Vyakhirev said that further listings would depend on the performance of Gazprom shares on the different bourses.
Gazprom shares listed on the Berlin stock exchange traded at 29.60 marks on Friday.

The financing deal follows a 1 billion mark Hermes covered facility, also led by Dresdner bank for Gazprom's Novy Urengoi project, as well as the issue of American Depositary Shares (ADS) worth nearly $430 million, co-led by Dresdner, in October of last year.
